items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, I worked there with Tad Dameron's band.

ctx.x: Yeah, I worked there with Tad Dameron's band. Thank you for mentioning that. I worked above with Tad, and he wanted -- he had an idea that he wanted a guitar lead on all of his -- most of his arrangements. So he wrote quite a few things and on top of all the voicings there would be the guitar. And as a matter of fact we did quite a few recordings with this, and one of the records won an award for the record of the year. It was called Focus and John's Delight, which I wrote.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Tadd and I were very dear friends

ctx.x: 1946. So Tadd Dameron, here we go. When I first met Tadd it was before I went in the army. Tadd came to New York to write for Lunceford, and we used to meet every night at the Woodside. We'd get high, we'd play, and you know -- so he would play these things, some of the arrangements he had for Lunceford and I would tell him, look, Tadd your ideas are beautiful but your bassline is wrong. So he said what do you mean, and so I would take just what he did and I'd play a different bassline, you know, and show him…

When I came out of the army, the whole scene had changed musically, so Tadd came and got me, and he said, come on, go to my hotel room, I want to show you something. So we had a little organ and he sat down and he started playing, he said this is the way things are going. And we would sit there all night and I would just listen and he would just play. And now, look, this is what has happened. He did this out of appreciation. He never forgot what I did for him. He said, here. So he would just play, he would just…
